CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS

18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, JULY 25, 2024,
7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

 5.  Presentations/Appointments

  matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Council/Agency members received full-text, unredacted copies of the five (5) written
  comments submitted for meeting items by the deadline listed on the agenda and for

  Clerk/Treasurer.

  Sunshine Park basketball court and requested to discuss the matter with members of

  Al Barlevy expressed concern regarding the conflict between Israel and Palestine.

  Gail Grossman expressed concern with lack of accessibility to the City Council Chamber.

  Coleen Aldrich expressed concern with lack of accessibility to the City Council Chamber
  and requested an update on the status of the Wildlife Watch program.

  City of Cerritos  July 25, 2024  $4,435,192.41 (COUNCIL)

7B.2. Approval of Fiscal Year 2023-24 budget amendments (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to authorize administrative-
  initiated Fiscal Year 2023-24 budget amendments in accordance with Joint Budget
  Resolution No. 2023-26/CSA No. 2023-01 and the Strategic Financial Plan and Budget
  Preparation Policy (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  1. Account/Project: cp13746 Arterial Landscaping at Various Locations
  Amount: $94,000
  Justification: Additional funding is requested for arterial landscaping
  improvements recently completed on 183rd Street between Shoemaker Avenue
  and Carmenita Road. This project, typically carried out alongside street,
  sidewalk, and gutter improvements, followed the asphalt repaving at this
  location. The work included installing new valves and couplers, sprinklers, and
  crape myrtle trees. These enhancements are essential to provide a polished,
  upgraded appearance to the newly improved stretch of road.

  2. Account/Project: 110-342-65172
  Amount: $80,270 (Transfer)
  Justification: A transfer of funds is requested for traffic signal maintenance. In
  addition to routine maintenance, the City encountered unforeseen maintenance
  costs and equipment failures related to traffic signal systems. These unexpected
  issues have increased the overall maintenance expenses, and the requested
  funds are necessary to ensure the proper functioning and safety of the City's
  traffic signals. This amendment proposes transferring the necessary funds from
  the sewer maintenance account to cover these additional costs.

  ;(COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.3. Approval of Fiscal Year 2024-25 budget amendments (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to authorize administrative-
  initiated Fiscal Year 2024-25 budget amendments in accordance with Joint Budget
  Resolution No. 2024-12/CSA No. 2024-01 and the Strategic Financial Plan and Budget
  Preparation Policy (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  1. Account/Project: 110-561-61580 Temporary Help
  Amount: $80,000
  Justification: A transfer of funds is requested to ensure the continued funding of
  temporary staff in the Management Information Services division following a staff
  retirement in February. The temporary staff has been essential in maintaining
  support for numerous enterprise applications and deploying various new Citywide
  enterprise systems. This amendment proposes transferring $40,000 from
  account 110-561-51010 (Regular Earnings) and $40,000 from account 110-561-
  52400 (Employee Benefits) to cover the cost of this critical temporary assistance.

  2. Account/Project: cp23201 CCPA Pro-Tower Safety Upgrade
  Amount: $80,197
  Justification: Additional funding is requested to install a powered drive system
  for repositioning the pro-towers. This system will allow a single staff member to
  control the movement using a remote pendant or joystick, with assistance from a
  few staff members, rather than relying on more than a dozen staff to manually
  push the structures. The powered drive system will enhance operational safety
  and efficiency beyond the original project scope and is expected to result in a
  labor savings of up to 14 staff hours per configuration.

  3. Account/Project: cp23118 Sports Complex Soil Restoration, Laser Grade and Sod
  Installation
  Amount: $180,000
  Justification: Additional funding is requested to cover the costs associated with
  a change order to install perforated drain pipes at fields 3, 4, 5, and 6 at the
  Sports Complex. This installation is essential to ensure proper drainage,
  specifically to leach out the high salt content present in the soil due to the
  reclaimed water system. The current soil quality and high salt content prevent
  adequate natural drainage. Installing the drainage pipes will promote the healthy
  growth and maintenance of the newly installed sod, ensuring the fields remain in
  optimal condition.

  4. Account/Project:  110-368-51010 Regular Earnings
  110-368-52400 Employee Benefits
  Amount:  $61,658 (Transfer)
  $10,925 (New Allocation)
  Justification: Additional funding is requested to reclassify a Management
  Analyst position (Grade 46) to a Utility Analyst position (Grade 49) within the
  Department of Public Works. Currently, there are two Management Analysts in Public
  Works: one assigned to the Director's Office and the other split between
  the Electric Utility and Water Utility.

  The position assigned to the Director's Office is currently vacant. This
  amendment proposes upgrading it to a Utility Analyst and reassigning it fully to
  the Electric Utility. Consequently, the Management Analyst currently split
  between the Electric Utility and Water Utility would be reassigned entirely to the
  Director's Office.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, July 25, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 10

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.3. (continued)

  This reclassification aims to dedicate a staff member exclusively to the Electric
  Utility. The funding for these changes will be covered primarily through transfers
  between the Director's Office, Water Utility, and the Electric Utility divisions,
  specifically $40,355 in Regular Earnings and $21,303 in Employee Benefits.
  Additionally, a new allocation of $10,925 in the Electric Utility division will be
  required.

  5. Account/Project:  110-551-52010 Regular Earnings - Part-Time
  110-368-52400 Employee Benefits
  Amount:  $45,662 (Transfer)
  Justification: A transfer of funds is requested to reassign a vacant part-time
  Human Resources Benefits Coordinator position from the Human Resources
  Division to the newly reconstituted Enterprise Services Division. This position will
  assist in the risk management side of Enterprise Services, specifically focusing on
  workers' compensation and related functions. This reassignment will be funded
  through a transfer in personnel expenditures between the Human Resources and
  Enterprise Services divisions, ensuring a seamless transition without additional
  budgetary impact.

  6. Account/Project:  110-551-52010 Regular Earnings - Part-Time
  110-551-52400 Employee Benefits
  Amount:  $152,557 (Transfer)
  $21,918 (New Allocation)
  Justification: Additional funding is requested to upgrade a vacant Division
  Secretary position in the Human Resources Division to a Management Analyst
  position in the Enterprise Services Division. This upgrade aims to enhance the
  oversight of employee relations, development, engagement, and performance
  management within Enterprise Services.

  The reclassification and reassignment of this position will bolster the operational
  capabilities of the Enterprise Services Division by providing dedicated support for
  critical administrative and managerial tasks. The funding for these changes will
  be covered primarily through transfers between the Human Resources and
  Enterprise Services divisions, specifically $77,440 in Regular Earnings and
  $75,117 in Employee Benefits. Additionally, a new allocation of $21,918 in the
  Enterprise Services Division will be required.

  7. Account/Project: 110-341-65090 Off Street Maintenance
  Amount: $208,190 (transfer from Fiscal Year 2023-24)
  Justification: Funding is requested for the repair work necessary to restore the
  operation of the water features in the Cerritos Towne Center area. The specific funding
  needs are as follows:

    Kamstra/183rd (West): $18,050
    Kamstra/183rd (East): $7,040
    Shoemaker/Park Plaza: $17,370
    Shoemaker/183rd: $18,020
    Gore (91 off-ramp at Shoemaker Ave): $147,710

  The majority of these water features were constructed over 40 years ago and
  now require extensive cleaning, major plumbing and electrical repairs, pump
  replacements, and other related component replacements. Additionally, some structural
  repairs are needed at the Gore water feature.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, July 25, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 10

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.3. (continued)

  It should be noted that this amendment was initially approved by the City Council
  on June 13, 2024, for the FY 2023-24 budget. However, due to unforeseen delays, the
  work has not yet commenced. Therefore, approval of this amendment is necessary to
  reappropriate the unexpended funds from FY 2023-24 to the FY 2024-25 budget.

  8. Account/Project:  110-541-51010 Regular Earnings
  110-541-52400 Employee Benefits
  Amount:  $172,280
  Justification: Additional funding is requested to establish a new Personnel
  Administrator position (Grade 48) in the Human Resources Division. This position
  will assist in the oversight of personnel management, recruitment, and employee
  benefits administration. The addition of this position is essential to enhance the
  efficiency and effectiveness of the Human Resources Division, ensuring comprehensive
  support for all personnel-related functions.

  ;(COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS SELECTING A REPLACEMENT STREET NAME FOR SQUAW VALLEY
  WAY, IN CONFORMANCE WITH CALIFORNIA STATE ASSEMBLY BILL 2022 (STATUTES OF
  2022, CHAPTER 479), REQUIRING THE REMOVAL OF THE TERM “SQUAW” FROM ALL
  GEOGRAPHIC FEATURES AND PLACE NAMES IN THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA*
  (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Sections 15061(b)(3) and 15378(b)(5) of the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines, this administrative activity is not a “project” under
  CEQA, and, even if it were, the proposed amendment is exempt from CEQA review.

  A staff report was given by Sabrina Chan, Advance Planning Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Sheila Gibbons expressed support for the selection of “Sun Valley Way” as the
  replacement street name for “Squaw Valley Way.”

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and adopt a resolution, formally selecting Sun Valley Way as
  the replacement street name for Squaw Valley Way, and selecting Deer Valley Way
  and Sky Valley Way as alternates, captioned as follows:

  Resolution No. 2024-16, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
  SELECTING A REPLACEMENT STREET NAME FOR SQUAW VALLEY WAY, IN
  CONFORMANCE WITH CALIFORNIA STATE ASSEMBLY BILL 2022 (STATUTES
  OF 2022, CHAPTER 479), REQUIRING THE REMOVAL OF THE TERM “SQUAW”
  FROM ALL GEOGRAPHIC FEATURES AND PLACE NAMES IN THE STATE OF
  CALIFORNIA (COUNCIL); and

  2. Direct City staff to pursue all legal avenues concerning reimbursement from the
  State for the City’s fulfillment of State mandates related to the renaming of Squaw
  Valley Way, inclusive of forming a coalition of municipalities to jointly pursue the
  reimbursement, and use said funds received to reimburse residents for related costs
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Martin Grossman expressed opposition to a proposed Charter amendment related to a

  Gail Grossman expressed opposition to a proposed Charter amendment related to a

  Mel Cortez expressed opposition to a proposed Charter amendment related to a directly

  Jay Gray expressed concern regarding the ad hoc working group process and expressed

  Celia Spitzer expressed concern with the ad hoc working group process, expressed

  Colleen Aldrich expressed opposition to a proposed Charter amendment related to a

  Kirit Chauhan expressed opposition to a directly elected Mayor and voter approval

  Al Barlevy expressed opposition to a proposed Charter amendment related to a directly

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Table any further consideration of a potential Charter amendment related to a

  2. Direct the City Charter Review Ad Hoc Working Group (Councilmember Barrows) to

  b. Conduct general “clean up” and modernization of the City Charter document

  ; and

  3. Present the results of the City Charter Review Ad Hoc Working Group’s review at a
  future public meeting for further review and consideration by the City Council
